gaps.sentence: You ___ have rushed the final checks — now there are errors everywhere.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' criticizes a past action with bad results: shouldn't have rushed.

gaps.sentence: You ___ not be so hard on yourself — everyone makes mistakes.
gaps.explanation: 'Should not' gives gentle advice against something: should not be.

gaps.sentence: You ___ bring your own laptop — we will provide everything.
gaps.hint: no obligation, so needn't not mustn't
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' means it is not necessary; 'mustn't' would mean it is prohibited: needn't bring.

gaps.sentence: You really ___ to apologise before this gets worse.
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' expresses advice similar to 'should': ought to apologise.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to wear a uniform at my last job, and I hated it.
gaps.hint: an obligation imposed in the past
gaps.explanation: Past obligation is expressed with 'had to': had to wear.

gaps.sentence: The lights are on and I can hear the vacuum cleaner, so someone ___ be at home.
gaps.explanation: Evidence-based certainty uses 'must': must be at home.

gaps.sentence: Sorry I am late — I ___ to take my car to the garage this morning.
gaps.explanation: Past obligation uses 'had to', since 'must' has no past form: had to.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ to buy the textbook; copies are available in the library.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' plus the infinitive expresses absence of obligation: don't have to buy.
